title: What is good: trust-domain callback architecture
description:
The three-callback trust-domain seam (SignatureVerifier + RevocationChecker + AiaFetcher) is a clean architectural choice worth defending:

1. Each callback has a zero-cost default (DefaultVerifier, NoRevocation, NoAiaFetcher) so callers pay only for what they use. The defaults are Copy types that inline to nothing.

2. The Verifier<'a, V, R, A> struct in pkix-chain packages slow-changing inputs once and exposes verify_one/verify_batch, separating setup cost from per-chain cost. The generic defaults (A = NoAiaFetcher) mean callers who don't need AIA fetching never name the parameter.

3. RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor has a default implementation (skip) with a loud security warning in the doc. This is the right trade: the default is safe for the common case (offline/embedded), and the doc makes the security gap explicit for full-chain-revocation callers. Both CrlChecker and OcspChecker override it, so production revocation implementations get automatic anchor coverage.

4. The callback trait surface admits caller-side caching by design (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6). A caching SignatureVerifier or RevocationChecker wrapper is a zero-change drop-in because the trait interface is the seam.

Locations: pkix-path/src/lib.rs (SignatureVerifier trait), pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs (RevocationChecker trait), pkix-aia/src/lib.rs (AiaFetcher trait), pkix-chain/src/lib.rs (Verifier struct, verify_chain free function).
